comments.author: Will
comments.text:
# Delta graft review notes — known mismatches + method (reference for dtx.1/.2/split-sibling cards)

Seed provenance: `saf generate delta -M` (PR #7971 build, §2-fixed re-seed at commit 074325b). Independent read-verification found the matcher's `potentialMismatch` flag has BLIND SPOTS — a graft can be confidently wrong:
- `related` and `fuse-fallback` grafts bypass the semantic check; a high `semanticScore` does NOT prove the body is correct.
- DISA reuses SRG/CCI tags across unrelated requirements, so even `srg-deterministic` grafts can be wrong.

Read-verified WRONG grafts (title vs what the carried body actually tested):
- SV-234845 — SLES "directory GROUP-owned by root"; source tested USER ownership (`! -user root`). [now empty -> split-sibling card: author fresh, check group ownership]
- SV-234975 — SLES audit records for `/run/utmp`; source audited `/etc/sudoers`. [now empty -> split-sibling card]
- SV-255921 — SLES "restrict the kernel message buffer" (kernel.dmesg_restrict); source tested sticky-bit on world-writable dirs. [now empty -> split-sibling card]
- SV-234964 — SLES "auditing package installed"; body is `package('sudo')` (from RHEL SV-258083). [flagged primary -> review card dtx.2: assert the audit package]

Method for the review/authoring cards: read each control's SLES check/fix text and confirm the body evaluates THAT requirement; never trust a graft because it parses or scored high. For dense SRG families (audit, PAM/password, crypto/FIPS) review the whole block, not just flagged members. Per-control match data lives in delta.json links[] (oldId, semanticScore, relationship, potentialMismatch).

title: Consolidate file-permission inputs into semantic hashes — SLES 15 profile
description:
## Phase 0 — MANDATORY REMINDER (read before every card)
**CORRECTNESS IS THE ONLY PRIORITY.** Best practices, standards, DRY, maintainable code — always. No shortcuts, no hacks, no workarounds. Card-close velocity is NOT a metric. Speed is NOT a goal. If an AC requires research, DO THE RESEARCH. If an AC requires a specific format, implement THAT FORMAT — do not substitute. Read the referenced context BEFORE writing code. Every AC gets evidence before close. The `/project-ac-verify` gate blocks `bd close` mechanically — an independent reviewer checks your work.

---

Title: Consolidate file-permission inputs into semantic hashes — SLES 15 profile

Description:
The profile currently expresses file-permission thresholds through a mix of ~7 near-identically-named scalar inputs (`ssh_pub_key_mode`, `ssh_private_key_mode`, `audit_conf_mode`, `audit_tool_mode`, `log_file_mode`, `initialization_file_mode`, `mode_for_libs`) plus two hashes (`expected_modes`, `modes_for_shells`), with two distinct semantics tangled together: "≤ this octet" ceilings vs. exact-per-file modes. This card consolidates the scalar ceilings (and the barely-used `expected_modes` stub) into coherent hash input(s) so operators tune permissions in one place instead of hunting a dozen look-alike variables — the pattern already used on our other SAF profiles.
Design doc: none — capture the chosen hash scheme in the card notes before migrating (see Decision points). Follows profile-development-rubric Phase 4b (generalize thresholds via inputs).

Files:
- Create: none
- Modify:
  - inspec.yml (define the new hash input(s); remove the migrated scalar inputs)
  - controls/SV-234832.rb (log_file_mode → new hash key)
  - controls/SV-234835.rb (mode_for_libs → new hash key)
  - controls/SV-234993.rb (expected_modes → exact-mode hash key)
  - controls/SV-234995.rb (initialization_file_mode → new hash key)
  - controls/SV-235008.rb (ssh_pub_key_mode → new hash key)
  - controls/SV-235009.rb (ssh_private_key_mode → new hash key)
  - controls/SV-235030.rb (modes_for_shells — fold into scheme or leave standalone; decide in Decision points)
- Test: none (profile validated via cinc-auditor, not a unit-test suite)

First failing test:
`cinc-auditor check .` after deleting the old scalar inputs from inspec.yml but before updating the controls → controls referencing the removed inputs must surface the break (or a `cinc-auditor exec` run showing the affected controls error). This proves every consumer was found before the migration is declared complete.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] The exact-vs-ceiling semantic distinction is preserved — ceiling ("≤ octet") thresholds and exact-per-file modes are NOT conflated into one ambiguous bag (see Decision points for the chosen scheme)
- [ ] All 7 scalar mode inputs (`ssh_pub_key_mode`, `ssh_private_key_mode`, `audit_conf_mode`, `audit_tool_mode`, `log_file_mode`, `initialization_file_mode`, `mode_for_libs`) are removed from inspec.yml and their values live under the new hash key(s), with defaults byte-for-byte unchanged
- [ ] `expected_modes` is migrated/renamed into the exact-mode scheme; `audit_conf_mode` and `audit_tool_mode` (currently referenced by zero controls) are still carried into the hash so the tunable is not silently dropped
- [ ] Each of the 6 consuming controls (SV-234832, SV-234835, SV-234993, SV-234995, SV-235008, SV-235009) reads its threshold from the new hash and its evaluated behavior is identical to before (same octet compared, same describe/failure output)
- [ ] Human-meaningful octets remain the input surface (e.g. `'0640'`), consistent with the existing convention
- [ ] `grep -rn "input('\(ssh_pub_key_mode\|ssh_private_key_mode\|audit_conf_mode\|audit_tool_mode\|log_file_mode\|initialization_file_mode\|mode_for_libs\)'" controls/` returns zero hits after migration
- [ ] All work via TDD (failing test first — the check/exec break above stands in for the unit test)
- [ ] No regressions: full-profile `cinc-auditor check .` → `Valid : true`, no new warnings; rubocop clean on every modified control
- [ ] Live tested: `cinc-auditor exec . --controls SV-234832 SV-234835 SV-234993 SV-234995 SV-235008 SV-235009 -t <target>` runs without profile errors and each control yields the SAME pass/fail verdict as before the refactor (before/after output pasted in card notes)

Verification:
`RUBOCOP_CACHE_ROOT=/private/tmp/rubocop-cache ~/.rbenv/shims/bundle exec rubocop --no-server --config .rubocop.yml controls/SV-234832.rb controls/SV-234835.rb controls/SV-234993.rb controls/SV-234995.rb controls/SV-235008.rb controls/SV-235009.rb` && `/usr/local/bin/cinc-auditor check .`

Decision points:
- STOP and confirm the hash scheme with the user before mass-migrating. Recommended (architecturally correct): TWO hashes — `max_file_modes` (ceiling `≤` semantics, keyed by logical class: `ssh_pub_key`, `ssh_private_key`, `audit_conf`, `audit_tool`, `log_files`, `init_files`, `system_libs`) and `exact_file_modes` (exact per-file/dir, absorbing `expected_modes`). The user framed it as "one giant hash" — if a single hash is preferred, it MUST still encode which entries are ceilings vs exact (e.g. nested sub-keys), never a flat bag.
- Decide whether `modes_for_shells` (logon/non-logon shell hash, SV-235030) joins the scheme or stays as a purpose-specific hash. It is already a hash with clear semantics; folding it in may reduce clarity — confirm before touching SV-235030.
- Renaming/removing public inputs is a breaking change for any downstream override files (`*.yml` passed via `--input-file`). Confirm no committed override files depend on the old names before deleting them.

Anti-patterns:
- Do NOT collapse ceiling and exact-match modes into one flat, semantically-ambiguous hash just because it is "one giant hash" — a key that silently means "≤" in one control and "==" in another is a correctness trap
- Do NOT change any default octet value while moving it — this card is a pure input refactor, behavior must be identical
- Do NOT drop the currently-unused `audit_conf_mode` / `audit_tool_mode` tunables just because no control consumes them today
- Do NOT add rubocop:disable to work around warnings — fix the root cause
- Do NOT close this card with any AC unchecked — no deferrals, no "lower priority" exceptions
- Do NOT optimize for card-close velocity or speed

NOT in scope:
- Authoring new controls or fixing delta-graft correctness (that is dtx.2 and the new-control work)
- The per-input "which controls use this" convenience comments in inspec.yml (separate background task; re-run that annotation AFTER this refactor lands since input names change)
- Broadening permission checks to files/paths not already covered by the existing controls
- Changing describe-block structure or failure messages beyond swapping the input source

Before closing:
- [ ] Re-read the Phase 0 preamble — correctness is the only priority
- [ ] **EVERY AC checkbox verified with evidence — NO EXCEPTIONS, NO DEFERRALS**
- [ ] Re-read Anti-patterns — confirm none violated
- [ ] Run the exact Verification command — paste output
- [ ] Live test proof pasted in card notes — before/after verdicts for all 6 controls against a real target
- [ ] Zero new linter disable comments in the diff
- [ ] AC verification gate resolved with evidence (never `--force` to bypass)
- [ ] git diff shows ONLY files listed in the Files section
- [ ] If closing 2+ cards in a row: STOP. Are you rushing? Verify each one fully.

Story points: sp:5
Estimate: 25

comments.author: Will
comments.text:
Highest-risk bucket to sweep first: primaries matched via `srg-cci-tiebreak`.

delta.json matchMethod distribution across the 214 links: srg-cci-tiebreak 170, srg-deterministic 26, fuse-fallback 10, none 8. Of the 193 `primary` grafts, **165 are srg-cci-tiebreak** — i.e. the matcher had no real semantic hit and fell back to "same SRG/CCI, pick one." That is exactly how SV-234937 (insmod) slipped in: RHEL9 has no insmod-audit control, so delta tiebroke to RHEL SV-258183 (the /usr/bin/chcon audit control) and grafted the chcon body onto the SLES insmod requirement. Wrong target AND wrong rule shape (syscall body on a `-w …-p x -k` watch requirement). Fixed 2026-07-10.

Review order recommendation:
1. The 15 potentialMismatch=True flags (already the known set).
2. The remaining srg-cci-tiebreak primaries — for each, diff the control's own `desc 'check'` text against what the body actually asserts. Tiebreak matches share an SRG/CCI but frequently test a different command/file/syscall than the SLES check demands.
3. srg-deterministic (26) and fuse-fallback (10) are higher-confidence; spot-check only.

Watch specifically for audit-rule grafts where `audit_command` / the watched path / the syscall list doesn't match the control title and check text — that mismatch class is invisible to lint and cinc-auditor check.

comments.author: Will
comments.text:
FULL AUDIT-RULE REVIEW COMPLETE (every control that checks an audit rule).

Scope: 50 controls touch audit rules — 47 use the auditd resource, 3 reference audit-rule syntax in check text (961, 962 = AIDE audit-tool integrity, correctly not rule checks; 981 = task,never).

Methodology: established the 3 canonical patterns from RHEL9 source (watch = exist+permissions+key [SV-258222]; program-exec = exist+action+list+fields(perm=x,auid)+key+auditctl -S all [SV-258194]; syscall = exist+action+list+arch+fields(auid)+key). Then two scanners over all controls: (1) body target vs check-text -w/-Fpath/-S target; (2) body assertion-set vs the canonical pattern for the control's check-text rule form.

Additional mismatches found + fixed in this pass (missed by the first target-only scan because its blind spot was check-text `-S all` program-exec and `-w` watch forms whose bodies were syscall):
- SV-234906: body auditd.syscall('umount') -> program-exec /usr/bin/passwd
- SV-234907: body auditd.syscall('umount2') -> program-exec /usr/bin/gpasswd
- SV-234913: body auditd.syscall(init_module,finit_module) -> dual -w watch /etc/sudoers + /etc/sudoers.d (-p wa)
- SV-234981: body checked kernel.core_pattern (+ wrong storing_core_dumps_required input) -> now asserts no "task,never" rule at runtime and in rules.d (matches its actual check text)

Also this session: the -S all auditctl line was RHEL-only cruft on the 4 module WATCHES (937/938/939/940) — removed, and those converted to the true -w watch pattern (permissions('x')+key). Verified legit on program-exec via RHEL SV-258194.

Final state: target mismatches 0; form issues 0 except two INTENTIONAL deviations — SV-234935 (umount b32-only + umount2 b32/b64, so no uniform arch assertion) and SV-234963 (execve -C uid!=euid/gid!=egid setuid/setgid, keys hardcoded). cinc-auditor check Valid:true, all rubocop-clean.

BROADER IMPLICATION: SV-234981's body was a core_pattern control — proof the srg-cci-tiebreak offset is NOT limited to the audit family. Non-audit families need the same body-vs-check-text scan. First suspect: SV-234904 ("audit records must contain information…") has a /etc/default/grub body — review in the audit-config pass.
